chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the son of a daughter and the daughter of a son. He said, 'Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) did not spare [effort] in giving the inheritance to the nearest [relative].' I said, 'Which of the two is nearer?' He said, 'The daughter of the son.'

So it follows the pattern of the first two reports in that it is not acted upon, because the rank of the daughter of the son is like the rank of the son of the daughter, so neither of them is nearer than the other. Therefore, the reasoning contained in the report spoils the report itself, and the explanation for it is what we mentioned in the first two reports.

key_terms.ابْنَةُ الْأَبْنِ: Daughter of the son (granddaughter via son)
key_terms.ابْنُ الْبِنْتِ: Son of the daughter (grandson via daughter)

ai.seo_question: Who is considered the nearer heir between the daughter of a son and the son of a daughter in Shia inheritance jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records Imam al-Rida’s (AS) observation that Imam Ali (AS) prioritized the daughter of the son in inheritance, yet the commentator critiques this as legally insufficient because the daughter of the son and son of the daughter hold equal rank, rendering the 'nearest' rationale self-contradictory. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of distinguishing between reported practices (*amali*) and binding legal proofs (*hujjah*), emphasizing that equal degrees of kinship require a more precise mechanism for distribution rather than arbitrary preference.
